[1;97mStage 1: Where am I?[0m

Five short lessons, then a task. You'll run your first commands and
learn the few keys that make a shell comfortable.

[93m▶ Type [92mnext[93m for lesson 1.1.[0m

[1;97mRunning a command[0m

A command is a name, then the words you hand it. [1mecho[0m is the simplest

one: it repeats its words back to you.

  [92mecho hello[0m                   [90m# prints hello, then the prompt returns[0m
  [92mecho I am at the shell[0m       [90m# spaces separate the words[0m
  [92mecho "I am at the shell"[0m     [90m# quotes make them one word[0m

Notice the quotes never print. They only group.

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m
echo I am at the shell
echo I am at the shell

[1;97mFour keys[0m

These keys make the shell comfortable. Try each one now.

[1mTab[0m       finishes a word: type [92mecho p[0m, press Tab, then Enter
  [1m↑[0m         brings back your last line; Enter runs it again
  [1mCtrl+C[0m    throws away the line you are typing; a fresh prompt
  [1mCtrl+L[0m    clears the screen; type [92mshow[0m to bring this lesson back

[1mCtrl+C[0m is the way out at a prompt. Inside a full-screen program
(you'll meet one in Stage 3) the way out is [1mq[0m.

[93m▶ Try each key, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mWhere am I, who am I, when is it[0m

The tutor made a folder for you to practise in. Ask the system where
it is, who you are, and what time it is.

  [92mpwd[0m        [90m# where: the folder you are in[0m

[92mwhoami[0m     [90m# who: your user name[0m
  [92mdate[0m       [90m# when: the date and time[0m

[92mpwd[0m prints the full name of your practice folder.
This prompt ends in [92m>[0m. An ordinary bash prompt usually ends in [92m$[0m.

[93m▶ Run all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mThe shell, caught in the act[0m

Type a real command, then the same letters scrambled.

[92mdate[0m     [90m# prints the date and time[0m
  [92mdtae[0m     [90m# bash: dtae: command not found[0m

[1mbash:[0m is the shell speaking. It looked for a program named dtae and
found none. A stray / in front or a missing space earns the same kind
of message: read it, then type the line again.

[1mterminal[0m → [1mshell[0m → [1mprogram[0m: the window, bash, and date.

[93m▶ Try both, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mWho else types here[0m

Every command goes terminal → shell → program. An AI assistant that
"runs commands" for you goes the same way: it types a line, the shell
finds the program, the program runs.

So three habits count twice, for you and for a helper:
  read the line before anyone presses Enter
  know which folder it will run in

read what comes back

Six short lessons, then a task. The shell is always standing in one

[1;97mWhere you are[0m

You are always standing in one folder: the [1mcurrent directory[0m. Here

is your practice folder, drawn as a tree:
  /var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-g_zs8eju  [93m◀ you are here[0m
  ├── poem.txt
  ├── numbers.txt
  ├── stage1/
  └── stage2/

  [92mpwd[0m        [90m# predict what it prints, then run it[0m
The line [92mpwd[0m prints is the full name of the "you are here" folder.

[93m▶ Run [92mpwd[93m, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mWhat is here[0m

[92mls[0m lists the names in the folder you are standing in.

  [92mls[0m            [90m# the names[0m
  [92mls -p[0m         [90m# the same, with / after each folder[0m
  [92mls -a[0m         [90m# also the hidden names, which start with a dot[0m
  [92mls /[0m          [90m# a folder you are not in: the top of everything[0m

Notice stage1/ in the second listing: the slash means a folder you
could step into.

[93m▶ Try all four, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

Applications	Volumes		etc		private		var
Library		bin		home		sbin
System		cores		opt		tmp
Users		dev		pkg		usr

[1;97mMoving[0m

[92mcd[0m changes the folder you are standing in. It usually prints nothing; [92mpwd[0m

shows where you are.

  [92mcd ..[0m      [90m# up one level, to the folder that contains this one[0m
  [92mpwd[0m        [90m# see where you are now[0m
  [92mcd -[0m       [90m# back to where you just were (it prints the place)[0m

[92mcd..[0m with no space is a different word, and bash cannot find it.

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mHome and back[0m

Every user has a home folder. [1m~[0m is its short name.

[92mcd[0m                 [90m# with nothing after it: go home[0m
  [92mpwd[0m                [90m# home is outside your practice folder[0m
  [92mcd /var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-g_zs8eju[0m

The last line uses your practice folder's full name. A full name works
from anywhere.

[93m▶ Go home and come back, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

A [1mpath[0m names a place. Three short names:
  [1m.[0m  here, the current directory    [1m..[0m  one level up    [1m~[0m  your home folder

A [1mrelative[0m path starts where you are: in ~/projects, the name notes
means ~/projects/notes. An [1mabsolute[0m path starts from /, the top:
/usr/bin is the same place wherever you stand.
  [92mcd stage1[0m      [90m# step into a folder[0m
  [92mls ..[0m          [90m# look one level up: your practice folder[0m
  [92mcd ..[0m          [90m# go back up[0m
  [92mecho ~[0m         [90m# ~ is a name: echo prints what it stands for[0m

[93m▶ Try all four, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[92mmkdir[0m makes a new folder inside the one you are standing in.

[1;97mReading a file[0m

[92mcat[0m prints a whole file at once.

[92mcat words.txt[0m          [90m# the word you put there[0m
  [92mcat hello.txt[0m          [90m# nothing: the file is empty[0m

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

The terminal is a quiet room.
You speak to it, it answers back.
Words have shapes here, and shapes have weight.
A pipe is a doorway between rooms.

[1;97mReading a long file[0m

[92mless[0m shows a long file one screen at a time. While it runs, the
prompt is gone: you are inside a program.

[92mless ../numbers.txt[0m    [90m# 50 lines, more than one screen[0m

[1mSpace[0m pages down, [1mb[0m pages back, [1mq[0m leaves. [1mCtrl+C[0m does nothing
here; [1mq[0m is the way out.

[93m▶ Open it, page down, press [1mq[93m, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mCopy and move[0m

[92mcp[0m copies and leaves the original. [92mmv[0m moves; the same command renames.

[92mcp hello.txt backup.txt[0m      [90m# now there are two[0m
  [92mmv hello.txt hi.txt[0m          [90m# rename[0m
  [92mmv hi.txt notes/[0m             [90m# move into the folder[0m
  [92mls -p notes[0m                  [90m# hi.txt is inside[0m

[93m▶ Try all four, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mStage 4: Commands and streams[0m

Six short lessons, then a task. You'll read a command's parts, then

join commands together and send what they print into files.
This stage runs in its own folder, stage4, with a few files the tutor put

[1;97mThe parts of a command[0m

A command line is a name, then options, then arguments.

[92mwc -l poem.txt[0m         [90m# name wc, option -l, argument poem.txt[0m
  [92mecho "hello world"[0m     [90m# one argument, because of the quotes[0m
  [92mcommand -v vim[0m         [90m# asks where a program lives, if it exists[0m

[92mcommand -v[0m prints a path when the program is installed, and nothing
when it is not.

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mSpaces and quotes[0m

The shell splits a line on spaces. Quote a name that has a space.

  [92mtouch my notes.txt[0m       [90m# two files: my, and notes.txt[0m

[92mls[0m
  [92mtouch "my notes.txt"[0m     [90m# one file with a space in its name[0m
  [92mls[0m

It is the same for every command: [92mvim my notes.txt[0m would open two
files; [92mvim "my notes.txt"[0m opens one.

[93m▶ Try them, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m
my		my notes.txt	notes.txt	poem.txt	seed.txt

[1;97mThe pipe[0m

What a command prints is a stream of lines. A pipe, [92m|[0m, sends that stream
into the next command.

[92mseq 1 100 | wc -l[0m              [90m# seq prints 1 to 100; wc -l counts the lines[0m
  [92mls /usr/bin | wc -l[0m            [90m# how many programs live there[0m
  [92mls /usr/bin | sort | head[0m      [90m# pipes stack: list, sort, first ten[0m

Each piece is an ordinary command. Only the connector is new. [92m|[0m is
[1mShift+Backslash[0m.

[1;97mInto a file[0m

[92m>[0m sends what a command prints into a file. [92m>>[0m adds to the end.

[92mecho first > greeting.txt[0m      [90m# writes over whatever was there[0m
  [92mecho second >> greeting.txt[0m    [90m# adds a line at the end[0m
  [92mcat greeting.txt[0m               [90m# two lines[0m

[92m>[0m replaces the file without asking, whoever typed the line.

[93m▶ Try all three, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mPipe, then file[0m

A pipe and a [92m>[0m work in one line: the last command's output goes to

the file.

  [92mls /usr/bin | wc -l > count-of-programs.txt[0m
  [92mcat count-of-programs.txt[0m      [90m# one number[0m

You'll do this in the task that follows.

[93m▶ Try both, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m

[1;97mMany names at once[0m

[92m*[0m matches any run of characters in a file name. The shell fills in

the names before the command runs.

  [92mls *.txt[0m         [90m# every name ending in .txt[0m
  [92mwc -l *.txt[0m      [90m# count the lines in each one[0m

A name with [92m*[0m in it is called a [1mglob[0m. Predict before you act: [92mrm *[0m
would remove everything in the folder.

[1;97mPrograms that take over the screen[0m

Most commands print and return. A few take over the screen until you

leave them; the prompt is gone while they run.

[1;97mLeaving Vim[0m

Vim is a text editor. Learn the way out before anything else.

[92mcommand -v vim[0m     [90m# a path means it is installed[0m
  [92mvim[0m                [90m# opens with no file[0m
